says: In next/, the law 'the bootstrap entry keeps the caller's span trace' fails with 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' whenever the L4 law before it times out: each world reads `Layer.buildWithMemoMap` into `buildLayer` (line 277) and then spies on it, and a world that never finishes never runs its `mockRestore`, so the next world reads the spy itself as `buildLayer` and its implementation calls itself.
proof: Failed in 4 runs on 4 different branches in 2 hours, each one right after L4 timed out at 60 s in the same job: https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/43586369357/job/132424559551 (t936-pipe-reads, attempt 1; the rerun went green), https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/43594434801/job/132445935994 (push to main; the next push to main went green), https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/43592894030/job/132441517020 and https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/43594995101/job/132448971235 (merge queue). Job 132424559551 prints `Caused by: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` at `Object.withParentSpan` (effect Layer.js:1991) called from runtime.laws.test.ts:281 three times over, after `L4 child grants ... 60031ms`. The fix is in flight: pull request https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/pull/1202 reads `Layer.buildWithMemoMap` once when the file loads, but it is DIRTY against main since the integration rename.
cost: One slow L4 run turns into several red laws that each look like a bug of their own, on any pull request or merge-queue group that reaches this file.
